title: Advertising as Information for Ranking E-Commerce Search Listings
eligible_reason: Not eligible. (i) The paper is a large-scale randomized field experiment at JD.com (abstract); treatment is random assignment of the ranking algorithm, not staggered adoption. (ii) The replication package stored under this suffix belongs to a different paper: its README and code analyze Numerator household panel data on online (Instacart) versus offline grocery trips (Section3_Table2.R, replication_fact_details.csv.gz, offline/online distance files) and state that the shipped data are simulated 50% draws with added noise. Nothing in the package relates to JD.com or advertising.
package_mismatch_note: Package contents (0.ReadMe.txt: 'We utilize proprietary Numerator data ... we offer simulated data'; R scripts Section2_Figure1.R ... Section4_Table8.R on Instacart/grocery trips) do not match the title/DOI. The correct package for Yang, Sahni, Nair and Xi (2023) needs to be re-downloaded from the INFORMS supplemental material page.
design_notes: From the abstract: field experiment at JD.com using ad-propensity information to rank new products; outcomes for platform and consumers. No staggered DiD design identifiable. The mismatched package runs fixest::feols regressions (Section4_Table8.R, Section4_Figure5.R) on simulated Numerator data for an unrelated paper.
estimators_reported: randomized_experiment (per abstract); package regressions belong to another paper
data_provenance: synthetic (mismatched package ships simulated Numerator draws with noise)
screener_notes: Flags ft_difference_in_differences/ft_staggered likely come from incidental mentions in the article. Action for lead: re-fetch the package for 10.1287/mksc.2021.0292 and identify which Marketing Science paper the current folder actually belongs to (Instacart/Numerator online-offline grocery comparison, R code dated Sept 2023).
